title: Saying It Again, Plainly: São Paulo

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *es decir*, *o sea*, *en otras palabras* and *dicho de otro modo* from B2 Unit 29. Each one says: "what comes next is the same idea, put another way." Writing about a big city needs them often, because a general line ("the city grew rich") is clearer once a second line makes it concrete. Here they work on São Paulo.

sections.title: Restating São Paulo
rows: São Paulo creció con el café; es decir, el dinero del café pagó el ferrocarril.
*es decir* brings the exact, concrete version
Llegaron inmigrantes de Italia y Japón; o sea, la ciudad se llenó de gente de muchos países.
*o sea* is the most spoken one
La Avenida Paulista era una calle de mansiones; en otras palabras, allí vivían las familias del café.
*en otras palabras* suits a longer, more careful sentence
Los obreros dejaron de trabajar; dicho de otro modo, hicieron huelga.
*dicho de otro modo* gives the idea a new label

items.spanish: El museo no tiene columnas en el centro; es decir, la plaza de abajo queda libre.
items.english: The museum has no columns in the middle; that is, the square below stays free.

items.spanish: Los barrios del ABC tienen muchas fábricas; o sea, allí trabajan muchos obreros.
items.english: The ABC districts have many factories; I mean, many workers work there.

items.spanish: São Paulo recibió inmigrantes de muchos países; en otras palabras, es una ciudad de origen mixto.
items.english: São Paulo received immigrants from many countries; in other words, it is a city of mixed origins.

sections.content: The new wording comes after the marker, and a comma or semicolon comes before it. Do not use these markers to add a new fact: for that you know *además* from A2 Unit 28. If the second part is the opposite of the first, you need a contrast connector such as *sin embargo*, not a restatement.
